findings.practical_consequence: The planner cannot preserve canonical sequence identity and discovery ancestry because every inventory row drops the registry lineage id.
evidence: operations/sequences/SEQUENCES.md defines lineage IDs; candidate sequence_inventory rows omit lineage_id although INV-001 requires it.

findings.practical_consequence: A planner could implement schemas against asserted interfaces that were never directly inspected.
evidence: Several callcenter, memory-knowledge, MAWF, and taggable rows cite representative sources rather than their exact executable or bundle.

findings.practical_consequence: The planner cannot derive one deterministic intake schema per executable because distinct entrypoints are collapsed into one sequence-level input description.
evidence: Multi-entrypoint rows have only one current invocation/input/no-arg/migration classification; wildcard and subcommand labels remain unresolved.

findings.practical_consequence: Direct argument-bearing paths could remain active and legacy compatibility cannot be distinguished from removable bypasses.
evidence: The candidate lists generic surfaces rather than exact path/anchor caller mappings and names no concrete machine compatibility consumers.
